annotation.title_clean: Navigating the sociotechnical labyrinth: Dynamic certification for responsible embodied AI
annotation.title_en: Navigating the sociotechnical labyrinth: Dynamic certification for responsible embodied AI
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Bakirtzis, G.; Aler Tubella, A.; Theodorou, A.; Danks, D.; Topcu, U.
annotation.summary_en: Book-chapter preprint proposing 'dynamic certification', an adaptive, iterative regulatory framework for embodied AI that links sociotechnical context, context of use and system behaviour. Certification starts with narrow approved uses and expands through monitoring, as in pharmaceuticals. An urban delivery robot is the worked example.
key_provisions_or_claims: Static regulation fits adaptive, opaque embodied AI poorly; dynamic certification is proposed instead.
Approval begins for narrow uses and contexts, then expands as safety evidence accumulates, as with drug approval.
Models, specifications and tests are living documents refined across early, transitional and confirmatory testing.
Continuous real-world monitoring helps detect bias, anomalies and context changes.
The framework is illustrated with an urban delivery robot and does not depend on a particular definition of AI.
